$comment: Decision register. 'evidenced' decisions cite the repository evidence they come from; 'newly-proposed' ones were made during implementation and are NOT owner-approved until TASK-CTX-0002 records the approval. Never invent a historical approval or rationale.

records.statement: Budgets are enforced in bytes; token figures are estimates at 3 bytes/token and labelled as estimates.
records.context: Packs must fit small context windows, but no tokenizer ships with the repository and token counts are model-specific.
records.selected: Byte budgets (schemas/config.json) with a conservative 3 B/token estimate shown next to them.
records.rationale: Bytes are exact and model-independent; 3 B/token over-estimates tokens for English prose (~4 B/token), erring towards smaller packs.

rejected.reason: adds a dependency and is still model-specific

history.evidence: Owner explicitly approved this decision in ChatGPT on 2026-10-22

records.statement: Graph edges are derived from record fields through schemas/relations.json; there is no separate edge file.
records.context: A dependency written on a record and an edge written elsewhere can disagree.
records.selected: Each relation declares which record fields emit it; the graph is rebuilt from the records on every run.
records.rationale: One fact, one place (Knowledge Once applied to the graph).

history.evidence: Owner explicitly approved this decision in ChatGPT on 2026-10-22

records.statement: Generated files carry the knowledge snapshot date (knowledge/state.json asOf), not the wall clock; wall-clock time is recorded only in receipts and handoffs.
records.context: Generated outputs are drift-checked byte for byte; a timestamp would make every build differ.
records.selected: generatedAt = state.asOf in packs and views; createdAt = now in receipts/handoffs (events, not projections).
records.rationale: Deterministic outputs make drift a real signal while events keep their true time.

rejected.reason: every rebuild would differ and drift detection would be meaningless

history.evidence: Owner explicitly approved this decision in ChatGPT on 2026-10-22

records.statement: Repository evidence is archived by git blob id + sha256 in the manifest; private exports go to a write-once content-addressed store outside git.
records.context: Original evidence must be preserved by bytes and restorable after the live file changes, without duplicating 2 MB of corpora or committing private data.
records.selected: git-blob / git-history storage kinds for repository evidence; 'store' kind (CONTEXT_ARCHIVE_DIR, default .context-archive/, gitignored) for private material.
records.rationale: Git's object store is already append-only and content-addressed; pinning the blob id makes every captured version restorable with `git cat-file`, so no second copy can drift. Private material never enters a public history.

rejected.reason: duplicates ~2 MB and creates a second copy that can drift

history.evidence: Owner explicitly approved this decision in ChatGPT on 2026-10-22

records.statement: Continuity knowledge lives in PROJECT-CONTEXT/knowledge/*.json; its markdown views and packs are generated; UCOS artifacts are imported read-only from _registry/manifest.json.
records.context: The system needs a canonical home for requirements, decisions, sources, tasks and context specs without competing with the constitutional registry.
records.selected: A separate PROJECT-CONTEXT/ tree, using the same projection pattern as _registry/ (authored JSON in, generated documents out).
records.rationale: _registry/ is the UCOS constitutional corpus: its files are inputs to the sealed compile (lib/canonical.js), so adding operational records there would change the seal and mix project-operations knowledge into constitutional content. A separate tree keeps one owner per concept and reuses the repository's proven pattern.

rejected.reason: changes the sealed compile's inputs and mixes operational knowledge into the constitution

records.statement: The existing .workbuddy-ai/memory/MEMORY.md is left untouched and archived as historical evidence; new continuity is recorded through schema-validated handoffs.
records.context: MEMORY.md is a 111 KB narrative ledger of sessions 2026-09-17 → 2026-10-07 and the only surviving record of those sessions.
records.selected: Archive it (SRC-MEMORY-LEDGER), cite its segments, and stop growing it as the continuity mechanism.
records.rationale: Rewriting or compacting it would destroy the only evidence of those sessions; as an unstructured narrative it cannot be checked for freshness or completeness.

records.statement: The continuity system uses only the Node standard library, including a small JSON Schema subset validator that rejects unsupported keywords.
records.context: Schema validation and hashing are needed; the platform minimises dependencies.
records.selected: Own validator (lib/context/schema.js) supporting exactly the keywords the schemas use; it throws on any other keyword.
records.rationale: No new install or supply-chain surface; a schema cannot claim a rule the validator silently ignores.

rejected.reason: new dependency for a small, fixed schema surface

records.statement: The registry (_registry/*.json) is the single source of truth and every constitutional document is a projection generated from it.
records.context: Hand-authoring 93 artifacts would define the same concept many times and drift on each retelling.
options: store truth in machine-readable registries and project documents
records.selected: Truth lives in _registry/*.json; node _registry/project.js projects the documents; node _registry/audit.js enforces the laws.
records.rationale: Hand-authoring would violate Law 002 (Knowledge Once); projection makes Law 003 executable.

rejected.reason: violates Law 002 — the same concept defined 93 times, drifting on each retelling

records.authority: repository constitution as committed (UCOS-REPOSITORY-INDEX.md); approver and date not recorded

records.statement: The corpora and registry JSON compile into one sealed canonical registry (lib/canonical.js) that the runtime reads; the seal is derived and reproducible, never stored.
records.context: Declarations were spread across the corpora and registry files with no single runtime source.
records.selected: node _registry/compile.js compiles, gates (five integrity criteria) and seals with AES-256-GCM + HMAC-SHA256 and a per-input sha256 manifest; the artifacts are gitignored.
records.rationale: One compiled, authenticated source makes drift and tampering detectable while keeping the sources as the authority.
records.authority: recorded in commit 7daf85b and the session-19 memory entry; owner approval not separately recorded
